text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER DV-610V-K MULTI REGION 1080p UPCONVERTING DVD PLAYER This is the most amazingly satisfying electronics product I have ever bought. The features are many and easy to learn. I especially enjoy some of the audio and video adjustment features:
Audio: DRC setting helps bring up quieter sounds while controlling loud peaks. Great for taming those annoying audio surges in 'background' music or battle scenes, etc. The Dialog feature lets you adjust the dialog perception so that you can hear the voices better over the background sounds in the soundtracks.
Video: You can adjust the Sharpness, Brightness, Contrast, Gamma, Hue, Chroma Level and BNR (block noise reduction). Each one has several levels to choose from and you get to sample it as it adjusts, so you can skip back and forth and compare the difference before you decide what to settle on.
The USB mode has great, easy to navigate menus. You can also record to your thumb drive from a CD that you are playing. There is a choice of different bit rates to do this and you can record individual tracks or all tracks. Very user-friendly menus for all these choices.
This unit has too many features to list, especially for someone like me, who is not quite fluent in tech terminology. Suffice it to say that it performs all the functions beautifully, the manual is very user-friendly and not only tells you how to adjust/change the various settings, but also explains the technical terminology in real English, so you know what those settings actually do when activated.
And if all that weren't enough, I scouted around a bit and bought the silver version (DV-610AV-S)of this unit for $30.00 less than the black one! (look for the one that ships for free with Amazon.com) Other than the color of the case, it is identical to the black one. I know, I looked them both up on Pioneer's web site and compared them point by point.
I do love the region-free feature too. But for me, this is more ho-hum, since I already owned one - a far inferior quality Philips one.
About the only thing I can think of to improve the user-friendliness of this product would be to have an alphabetized index in the manual. But, since it's only a 61 page manual, it's not such a big issue overall.
Another suggestion I would have would be to allow to record audio from DVDs also. So often, the audio track on a DVD sounds so much better than the soundtrack that is published on CD (i.e.: Brassed Off, Eyes Wide Shut), although I recognize there may be some copyright issues with that concept.
For the record: I am getting a second unit for my upstairs TV. Have I mentioned that I love it...? This is a really great product!!!
P.S.: Adding this comment on Jan. 17, 2010: I see the price difference between the black and the silver model is now up to $90.00!!! The silver one is the very same model, folks, but $ 90.00 cheaper!!! I am still just as enthused about this player as I was when I first reviewed it. I now own 2 units. Superb product!!!
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER DV-610V-K MULTI REGION 1080p UPCONVERTING DVD PLAYER

text_fidelity_a:
TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player Update. April 12, 2014. 4 months after purchase.

I have unplugged the TIVO, will pay the monthly fees for the next 8 months. At least I'll save the $ 3 month cable card fees.

I got another tuner. The tuner works. I have 2 TIVOs and the new tuner works in the old TIVO, but not the new Roamio. It is a Roamio problem.
I now only get 4 standard def stations with the Roamio.

TIVO offered to replace the Roamio for a flat $ 49, plus shipping. I figure the total cost will be $ 75. I'm sure I will get a refurbished TIVO.
Decided it wasn't worth spending $ 75 to get a refurbished TIVO, which may or may not work. Since my ROKU 3 gives me Time Warner Demand channels, it is much less compelling to have a TIVO.

I'll keep the TIVO Premiere connected as it has a lifetime and is trouble free, The Time Warner demand capability of the ROKU 3 is a major threat to TIVO's existence.

I did purchase the TIVO on Amazon with the AMEX credit card which doubles the warranty. I called AMEX. Was told it would not cover the cost of the replacement ($ 49). Only would cover the labor cost, since parts were still under the TIVO warranty (90 days labor, 1 year parts). Since labor isn't separately charged, I'm not covered. Think that stinks.

Update. 105 days later.

Well warranty is up by 15 days. TIVO doesn't recognize tuning adapter. My old premiere works perfectly.
Time Warner spent 2 hours at my home today, swapped out cable cards and tried 3 different tuning adapters. It's a TIVO issue.
I bypassed tuning adapter for a direct hookup. Gives me half the channels. When my one year committment is up, I'll scrap it.

Only saving grace. When I called to cancel my 13 month old Premier XL, they offered me a lifetime for $ 199. I took it.
Do not recommend it Roamio. I was one of the original TIVO users. A 45 hour standard definition TIVO. Very disappointed.

Original review.

Integrated Wi Fi. It's about time. This is my 4th TIVO. Currently paying for 2 monthly subscriptions. Have been satisfied with all my TIVOs. Getting rid of the $ 90 Wi Fi accessory is a big plus. Our other TIVO is a 2 tuner Premiere XL that holds 300 hours of HD. We've never had it over 25% , so 75 hours is enough for us. Our other TIVO has been moved to the bedroom. We really needed at least a 4 tuner set. Two tuners may seem enough, but the stations are now playing it cute by ending programs at 9:01 instead of 9. This causes a conflict and forces you to cancel a show, or not watch a live station at the same time. It effectively reduces the two tuner to a one tuner. Before your TIVO arrives, go to your cable source (if you use cable), and get the appropriate cable card for a 4 tuner set, and tuning adapter. TW charges me $ 2.80 each for the cards. One for each TV. You need to call your cable company to activate and pair your cable card. TW has a great system, and it took only minutes to do. You also need to have an HDMI cable on hand, and a USB to HDMI cable. The kind that connects from your wired printer to your computer.

I also pay monthly, not lifetime. On my original TIVO, an old 45 hour SD job, I took a $ 199 lifetime plan after 2 months. Three weeks later, a nearby lightning strike wiped out the modem on my TIVO, and my computer. Yes, I did have surge protectors, as well as a $ 300 whole house surge protector sold and installed by my electric company. End of my TIVO, end of my $ 199 lifetime plan. TIVO offered no sympathy. So TIVO yes. Lifetime plan NO.

You cannot stream to your mobile devices with the 4 tuner TIVO, without adding accessories.

Added. You also need a short coaxial cable. My prior TIVO packages included every possible cable you may need. No longer. The power supply, remote, remote batteries, and the TIVO were all that were included. An added explanation on the usb needed. The standard side of the USB connection connects to the TIVO. The printer type side connects to the tuning adapter. I went to my junk box, and pulled an old printer cable out. It's not the older type with the large ends. It is a very small odd sided type that plugs in. The cable company should be providing these. Ask them for one.
text_fidelity_b: TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player

That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down.

This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card.

Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it.

As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me.

Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

text_fidelity_a:
Mohu Leaf Glide Amplified Indoor TV Antenna, 65-Mile Range, UHF/VHF Multi-directional, Paper-Thin, 16 ft. Coaxial Cable, 15dB Amplifier with USB Cable, Reversible, Paintable, 4K-Ready, MH-110925 My high hopes for this antenna were quickly dashed.

I am 43 miles away from the broadcast towers. I currently use the Marathon antenna (I use it indoors). The Marathon picks up all the major network channels perfectly except occasionally 1, and all the independent stations perfectly except occasionally 1. (It will pick up those 2 stations, but there is sometimes annoying pixelation and signal drops.)

So, after I read how this brand new Mohu Leaf Glide 65 Mile Range antenna was supposed to be so wonderful, I bought it, hoping I could get all the stations in perfectly.

It's awful! Placed exactly where the Marathon was placed the Leaf Glide cannot even come close to picking up as many stations. And yes, I made sure the amplifier was plugged in. And it is getting power. (It also could not pick up stations that cheaper/inferior antennas could.)

I moved the Leaf Glide to different spots, but no matter where I placed it it could not pick up stations that it should have been able to pick up. It picked up some stations, so I know the amp was working. I unplugged the amp and those stations were gone, so I know it is not a defective amp.

I know that when it comes to antennas people's results will vary. But for this $89 (current price) supposedly "new technology" antenna to fail so badly is a huge disappointment.

There is no doubt that this antenna will work perfectly for many people, if they are lucky when it comes to distance, terrain, height, interference, etc.

You would think in today's world of big technology there would be a way to broadcast signals that everyone can receive successfully.

My guess is that this antenna would only pull in 65 miles away if one had it outdoors, high up, and with clear line to the towers.

(I am in no way affiliated with the company that makes the Marathon. I am just a cord cutter trying to get all the stations received perfectly. If the Leaf Glide had worked I would have been so happy, and would have gladly done away with the Marathon since it is quite big and not the most attractive. The Leaf Glide is paper thin and not anything that would be something you would not wanna look at.)

The Leaf Glide is very easy to place. I appreciate that they included two easy ways to hang it: Either with white or black push pins or with velcro sticky dots.

If you get all the stations with this antenna you will love it.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Leaf Glide Amplified Indoor TV Antenna, 65-Mile Range, UHF/VHF Multi-directional, Paper-Thin, 16 ft. Coaxial Cable, 15dB Amplifier with USB Cable, Reversible, Paintable, 4K-Ready, MH-110925

Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Black They seem to have put a lot of effort into this case to make it as 'fancy' as possible - it's not just a 'put the kindle in the elastic tabs and close the flap' type, that's certain. When I opened the package, I had to check the description a few times to assure myself that it was leather, as it's rather hard to the touch (I'm sure it makes it nice and durable, and it helps with both protection and standing up the kindle). What I like about the case is that it's rather slim, keeping your kindle protected without adding a lot of bulk to it (good while traveling), and that there are real buttons where the on/off and volumn buttons are on the kindle hd (so it offers some more protection there). Your kindle 'snaps' into the case and it's not too difficult to put it in and out.

As for the origami folding, it was pretty easy to get it to go into landscape mode. At first I thought that was ALL it could do. It wasn't easy to get it to stand portrait-style, and I'm not convinced that it's very stable this way, to be honest. I still have to play with my cover to get it to 'fold' right for portrait and it doesn't seem to fold as neatly, but maybe that's a personal issue. Also, this works best on flat, stable surfaces.

It tells you on the directions that you're going to have to slide the kindle hd out in order to take a picture. So if you're planning on using the camera a lot, that might get very annoying.

All in all, it's a sturdy cover with magnetic closure that will put your kindle hd into sleep mode but won't add too much bulk and seems to offer decent protection, and does offer some display capability (ymmv). Because it's not as thick, I don't have as much problem folding it back to hold it and read, but there is the odd texture because of the folds (so another thing to consider). I like this cover - it's not perfect, but I think it's pretty good. But there are some quirks that people should probably consider in light of its price.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Black

- one speaker unit with both left and right speakers inside the large housing

The sound this produces when I play my CDs was awesome and music to my ears. I also paired this speaker with my Google Nexus 7 Tablet (2013 version Android device) and my iPad Pro 12.9 and experienced moderately powerful sound there as well. The FM radio was staticky but that was due to the location of where I placed my unit. When I did receive a station, the sound was great.

In summary, this produces beautiful sound. As a Bluetooth speaker, it does not produce as powerful a sound as my [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Block Rocker]] but it is still good. The addition of the FM radio is a nice touch. I also like that it functions as an LED clock. The instructions and operation of the unit take a bit of getting use to and can be confusing but I was eventually able to figure it out; although I may have to consult the pamphlet every now and then. Overall, this is a well-rounded unit for indoor use but the unit is larger than I expected. It is as large as those old AM/FM amplifiers from years ago and has a retro 70’s look (see attached picture).

PS For those who are interested in comparisons, this is my sixth Bluetooth speaker. I ordered five other Bluetooth speakers over a several year period. I have a [[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]], which is not very good and a [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] which does not work when paired with some devices and, when it does pair well, it usually lacks the powerful sound I am looking for.

I also purchased one [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Audio Block Rocker (iPA76A) | Portable Bluetooth Speaker]] and one [[ASIN:B01N17AQ7U ION Audio IPA88 Tailgater Flash Wireless/Bluetooth Speaker]] both from Costco. I absolutely love the Block Rocker (except for when paired with my iPad Pro) and I only like the Tailgate Flash. The lights on the Tailgate Flash annoy me because they have to be turned off every time I power on the unit. Nevertheless, the sound from the ION speakers are usually awesome. The IONs are the only ones I use frequently indoors (even though they are more of an outdoor Bluetooth speaker). They are battery powered powerful speakers and the sound is intense. If one wants Bluetooth only with the capability of travelling with them without having to find a power outlet, then these are worth considering.

I also have a [[ASIN:B01MUG5WIN Sony XB20 Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth, Blue (2017 model)]] which pairs well with my HP Omen Laptop and moderately well with my Nexus 7 and iPad Pro. However, this has to be charged first just like the Goal Zero speaker that I dislike.

PS My boyfriend connected his iPad 3 to this one's Bluetooth and loves it for listening to Podcasts. In order to get the volume as loud as he wanted, he also used the volume controls on the side of his iPad in conjunction with the volume knob on the Toshiba. On another note, he mentioned that the controls located below the CD player are very small for someone who has eye problems and I would agree with that. What I find inconvenient is that the button to open and close the CD player is there so that when the CD is open, I have to put my hand underneath it to close if I am not using the remote. Nevertheless, he loves this Toshiba just like I do.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).
text_fidelity_b: Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite I haven't had this for very long yet, so I can't comment on longevity, but so far I like it. I take it for granted that there will be some sacrifices when using this type of mouse, I just don't expect to get the same flexibility and usability in terms of various buttons and their placements, so I can't really knock it for being a bit worse in that area than some regular, non-ergonomic options. It works very well and the buttons are easy to click and have a nice "click" to them (unlike cheaper ones). Of course, it takes some time to get used to an upright mouse if you haven't used one before, but after a while it becomes easy/natural.

Regarding the wrist angle, I had some wrist pain and in the past I'd used a cheaper upright ergonomic mouse to help. This is not carpal tunnel, I get joint inflammation on the top side of my wrist, so it may be a bit unusual.
When my old ergonomic mouse broke I decided to try a more expensive one in hopes it will last longer. I can't provide any definitive conclusions on whether this particular aspect of my "treatment" really does anything. My ultimate conclusion is that while treating with other things (e.g. braces, compression, cold or hot), using an alternate device sometimes to change the stress points probably doesn't hurt. Sometimes when going back to use my normal mouse, just putting my hand into position seems to cause some strain, so I think this upright position is helping some. But my experience is that if I use anything for too long, I'll find some joint and/or muscle getting stressed. I'm concerned that this upright mouse position may not be as good for my elbow. So my conclusion is mix it up to spread out the strain rather than hammering on a single weak area, and try to be more careful in the future to start treatment sooner, when I see the early warning signs of strain, before it gets bad.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite

text_fidelity_a:
JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”
text_fidelity_b: JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this drive provides speeds approaching the highest-end built-in SSDs. Case in point: I have a 2018 MacBook Pro with top specs. Its internal SSD is a screamer. And, as you can see from my screen shots, the X5 is right in the same neighborhood. These tests were run on my computer while it was running a bunch of other things (Word, Excel, VMWare Fusion, Mail.app, Safari with about 15 tabs open), so it represents real-world use.

And, as you can see, the X5 is really fast. If you need speed and have Thunderbolt 3, this is a great drive.

Installation was easy. My Mac recognized the drive right away. I could've just used it, but Samsung provides a utility on the drive for enabling its onboard encryption and keeping its firmware up to data. Recommended.

(But do make sure your computer has Thunderbolt 3. You can't tell just by looking at the ports, as TB3 is implemented as a superset of USB-C. So, Thunderbolt 3 is USB-C but the converse is not true. Similarly, previous-rev Thunderbolt interfaces aren't forward-compatible to TB3 devices. Some of the one-star reviews of this drive are clearly from folks who didn't know these issues.)
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

text_fidelity_a:
Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB) This is an unremarkable USB drive, with unexciting performance, for an unattractive price. (That's pretty much it for the substance of the review.)

I do my tests on a pretty fast computer with tons of memory, and an SSD system drive, while I'm doing nothing else on the computer, so no system resource constraints should affect the results. I test writes from SSD to USB, and reads in the other direction. I also use a set of 2GB test files, so that I get true results (small files can give misleading results).

I saw writes to the USB drive going between 4.5 and 8 MB/s, which is really pretty slow. I can get 16+ consistently on a little Lexar 32GB drive I have lying around. And a quick look in Amazon shows that I can find much faster USB3 drives for a bit less or a bit more, promising about 5x the write performance.

Finally, the form factor is terrible. This is a big fat ugly drive, you can get higher capacity and much better performance in slim little drives, including nano-drive size products.

Bottom line, it's ok, but I can't recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB)

However, the actual speed that it delivers is < 300 Mb /s.

I wasted a lot of time investigating this. It turns out that the reason why is because this device wrongly claims to be a USB 3 device (capable of 5,000 Mb / s) but acutally connects to my computer as a USB 2 device (merely 480 MB / s in theory, but in reality always less than this).

This defect turns out to be mentioned in several Amazon review that I I wish that I had noticed, and is discussed on TP-Link's forums.

text_fidelity_a: Sony MDRNC7/BLK Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones (Black) My husband and I bought two sets of these three years ago from Circuit City during their going out of business sale. We both travel quite a bit and were in need of decent headphones for longer flights (let's face it, the ear buds provided by the airlines just don't cut it). My husband accidentally left his set, in their pouch, in the seat back pocket on a flight last year and was in need of a replacement set for our trip to Germany last week. I was amazed by the price when I came onto Amazon to check - $29.99 was a steal compared to the $80 we spent a few years back! This headset is not the top of the line, but it is effective in canceling out the low aircraft drawl while in-flight. (They are also quite nice when you need to drown out the crying child in 23F. ;)) The battery life is remarkable. I have had to change the battery on my set only twice in the three years I've owned it. The only complaint that I have, which results in the four star rating instead of five, is that after wearing the set for a few hours (i.e., Amsterdam to Houston, TX), my ears begin to ache on the outside. It is almost like the headset becomes to tight over longer periods of time. I tend not to wear earrings on airplanes, so I can rule out the possibility of pinching. Other than that slight achy feeling, these are wonderful for the casual traveler and the price simply cannot be beat!
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRNC7/BLK Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones (Black)

I decided to upgrade from my Logitech G430 headset. I was mainly looking for a wireless headset that had great battery life, great sound and did not cost too much. Even without the deal, the $200 price point is still reasonable compared to other wireless headsets. I was considering the Corsair and Astro's before purchasing this one. I am using this headset for my PC only, to game.

The Headset:
- Customizable buttons to change the Equalizer, play/pause, and many other options to choose from
- Convenient volume dial to change sound on the fly. This is great so you dont have to minimize the game and adjust the volume settings with the mouse
- Headset grips my head. I have an angled forehead which my old headset would easily slide off when moving around
- Comfy ear pieces that does not cram my ears and feel uncomfortable
- Comes with long braided charging cable, AUX cables, and RCA cables
- USB adapter to connect the wireless headset it plug and play. You just need to make sure you install the Logitech dashboard to customize the headset
- The Logitech logo and a line down each ear-cuff lights up. To me this is a pointless feature as I am wearing the headset and cannot see the lighting and only uses up battery life. I disabled the lights and my battery life increased by 3 hours.

Sound:
The sound i will say is significantly better than my G430. There are multiple equalizer profiles to choose from (FPS, Cinema, etc.). Once you turn on surround sound and 7.1, it makes a big difference of sounds. You can change the treble, bass, and customize the sound to your liking.

Battery:
I cannot say too much about the battery life, but after a full charge, and turning off the leds on the headset. It said I have 12 hours of battery left. After wearing the headset playing Battlefield 5 for 4 hours, I still had 93% battery life. Overtime with charges and draining, i would assume the life would degrade a bit and would get around 10 hours of battery. I did not check how long it takes to charge the headset from a full depletion.

The only cons I have are the pointless LED lights if you are not showing off your headset. I do feel the headband part of the headset is not as strong as I would have expected it to be, just do not twist headband much.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G933 Artemis Spectrum – Wireless RGB 7.1 Dolby and DTS Headphone Surround Sound Gaming Headset – PC, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, and Mobile Compatible – Advanced Audio Drivers – Black

Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.
text_fidelity_b: Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming

Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa, 8" HD Display, 32 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th) I guess I'm a little bit of a Fire-omaniac in that I own 3 different Fire tablets; an old 7" that I use primarily to play solitare; a 10" that I use with a keyboard as a small laptop and now this New 8" Fire HD. I traded in a Fire 6" for this . The 6" , I felt was just a little small. It's amazing what an extra 2" can do! This Fire fits perfectly in the murse that I bought in Italy last year.
So much for fashion, but how does it perform? Well, the screen definition is bright, sharp and clear. I LOVE the Blue Shade feature for night time reading in bed. I'm impressed with the audio quality of the two small speakers. As a professional musician, sound quality is important to me. The option of using an SD card for extra storage of music and photos is also a valuable asset.
The tablet responds very quickly, is easy to navigate and simple to use. I bought it for travel but find myself using it at home in place of my laptop.
The only slightly disappointing feature are the on-board cameras. The photos are a little grainy.
All in all, it's a great tablet. My wife likes it so much that she wants one as a substitute for her iPad.

TP-Link AV1200 Powerline Ethernet Adapter - Gigabit Port, Plug&Play, Power Saving(TL-PA8010 KIT) Ordered at 7am PDT
Received at 5pm PDT
Plugged it in with the very very simple 6 step instruction. Don't let this fool you though. It's as easy as plugging in a cord into an outlet.
( note: do not use a power strip. It must be plugged directly into the wall.

No additional configuration was necessary. it just started working.

background: I needed this for my ps4, which is about 40 feet away from the router and hits 2-3 walls. I get about 300Mbps with Spectrum, but down at the 2.4 frequency. I can receive about 40-50Mbps depending on the strength of the the radio card on the device. The original PS4 wifi card is notorious for being extremely poor in quality. I was receiving about 2Mbps down and 599Kbps up. Yes, you read that right. a modern PS4 on a 2.4 frequency was getting shitty thruput. While at the same time, my other devices on a 2.4 frequency were receiving 10x that, even more on a 5g frequency.

I plugged in this unit and immediately got 10Mbps down and 5Mbps up. It's not a game changer, but will suffice.
Update after 12 hours: Reset the modem and did another speed test on the ps4. 25Mbps down and 10Mbps up.

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control After searching review after review for a router with solid performance and features I ended up with the N66. I am not a networking professional but I can tell you there is an enormous difference between a good N900 router and an N300 router you may have gotten from your ISP. I would take any review that is not written by a professional with a grain of salt but here's my 2 cents.

I live in a densely populated area with 20+ Wi-Fi networks with decent strength AND I live in a brick building. I have 50 Mps/down from my ISP and with this router I am able maintain at least 50 Mps throughout my ~900 ft2 apartment with one exception, the back porch. Speeds dip to about 15 Mps on the back porch on both the 2.4 & 5 Ghz bands, as I understand it Wi-Fi doesn't get along with brick. There is a brick wall in between my the rest my house and and finally my router. Understandable.

The takeaway, if you need a fast router, I think you will be hard pressed to find a better one. I haven't even touched on USB support for printers, USB applications & external storage, VPN, iOS applications, etc.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control

text_fidelity_a:
ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.
text_fidelity_b: ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded) In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable.

The pros:
• The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms.
• The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks.
• It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana.
• The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward.

The cons:
• While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding.
• The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do
• The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many.

After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded)

text_fidelity_a:
YOTON 12.5" Portable DVD Player with 10.5" HD Swivel Screen for Car and Kids, with Car Charger and AC Adaptor, Supports 4-6 Hours Built-in Battery and USB/SD Card/Sync TV [Not Support Blu-Ray] Recently, I have wished that I had the ability to watch DVDs in bed without having to watch on the big TV. I also would like to take it to my shed with no electricity so that I can play art classes without having to rely on internet at all.

HOW THIS CHARGES
This charges using the type C cord in a few hours.

PICTURE
The picture is decent. It is not like watching an expensive bluray or TV screen, but it is fine for close up watching.

OPERATION
I have had no issues operating this. It is pretty easy and the set up is not difficult to adjust.

SOUND
That is where we lose a star. Even at the highest setting of 20 this is so quiet that if I run fans in the summer, it is hard to hear with the player right in front of me. Headphones would solve that, but I don't always want to wear them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I like this set. It is fun to play with and allows me to watch my English tribute of nightly Hyacinth Bucket episodes where no one else has to listen to it and complain because I play it too much.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If the sound was a little bit louder and better, I would like this more. As it is it is still okay.
text_fidelity_b: YOTON 12.5" Portable DVD Player with 10.5" HD Swivel Screen for Car and Kids, with Car Charger and AC Adaptor, Supports 4-6 Hours Built-in Battery and USB/SD Card/Sync TV [Not Support Blu-Ray]

text_fidelity_a: Sanus Adjustable Height Speaker Stand - Extends 28" to 38" - Holds Satellite & Small Bookshelf Speakers (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, Polk, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony and Others) - Set of 2 - Model: HTBS First step per instructions is to detach 10 felt pads, one at a time, from the paper backing and place them on the 10 legs (5 each) on the bottom of the 2 heavy metal base pieces. What a pain as these fiddly little felt pads don't detach easily from the backing. And are so small they are hard to position on the legs just right. Black on black. Hard to see. And why 5 when 3 bigger ones would do it? I have bought desktop computers and other items with the rubber feet already installed. Why not these? What would it cost the manufacturer? Peanuts. Aluminum pipes screw together fine but when the speakers are installed, with the base oriented as per instructions, whole thing pitches forward. Solution: orient the bases in the opposite direction and the balance is better. Better not perfect. To get a straight up balanced posture, the bases will have to be shimmed in front. Not the end of the world but still. Tip: during assembly, ignore instructions and attach speakers to the upper pipe alone and then insert the upper pipe into the lower pipe and tighten down the friction-fit as needed. Much easier than wrangling the whole assembly with heavy base attached. And I wonder if this system will hold the speakers solidly to permit the full bass sound to be projected. Won't these flimsy pipes allow the speaker to vibrate and so loose sound energy projection? Much better would be mounting the Polks on the wall (for resonance) but this was not an option.

Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 50 Ft White Flat 40Gbps High Speed Shielded RJ45 LAN Cable I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

text_fidelity_a:
COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019 This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019

text_fidelity_a:
OTTERBOX DEFENDER iPhone 6 PLUS/6s PLUS Case - Frustration FRĒe Packaging - BLACK This is our fifth OtterBox, dating back to my I phone 3GS. This version has a major improvement,

Pros.
1. The plastic screen finally looks good. There was always a gap between the screen and the I Phone glass. That gave it a cheap look. That gap is gone. The plastic screen goes flush against the I phone glass and looks much better.
2. We have never dropped our phones, but this case gives us a great feeling of security. At $ 800 or so per phone, it's really cheap insurance.

Cons.
1. Installation and removal. We don't install these often enough to remember how to do it. The case comes assembled, and must be disassembled before use. Couldn't remember how to disassemble it. I finally went to You Tube to watch a video. Search term: "installing an OtterBox case." A comment to the video jogged my mind. It's like changing a bicycle tire. I used a miniature screwdriver to separate the rubber from the case at the corner. Nothing sharp. The rest of the rubber came off easily. The plastic parts separated easily enough. Place the phone inside, after cleaning both screens. Click the plastic pieces together, then place the rubber on. Keep massaging the rubber until it fully envelopes the plastic tightly. Had a few gaps at first.

2. Takes away the looks of the I Phone. Steve Jobs must have hated OtterBox.

3. Apple has a neat stand up charger for about $ 35. I bought one. OtterBox was late to the party with the OtterBox 6 plus, so I purchased the Apple 6 Plus leather case. Not much protection, but looks sharp. Worked great with the Apple stand up charger. Looked sharp together. Unfortunately, neither the OtterBox, nor any case that recesses the apple phone insert will work with this charger. Only a very thin shell will work with the charger. Back to using the regular Apple cord. I also have the OtterBox Strada for my I Phone 6. I like it. Although much thinner than the Defender, it doesn't work with the stand up apple charger either. Looks great. Many compliments. For those that don't like to carry a wallet all the time, the Strada has a pocket that contains both my license and one credit card. Great for trips to the gym. My wife has the Defender.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX DEFENDER iPhone 6 PLUS/6s PLUS Case - Frustration FRĒe Packaging - BLACK

ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White I replaced a large bulky router/modem combo from my ISP with this modem, as I already had a good router and didn't need two routers. My ISP was charging roughly $10 a month for their equipment, which I will save now. Of course the SB8200 is a little bit pricey, so it will take me about one and half years to recover my cost. I was surprised how small this modem is; very compact and easy to find space for. It generates a little heat, but has vent holes all over the outside and top for good ventilation. Most of heat come out the top, but obviously you don't want to block any of the openings and make sure there is plenty of space above it. I am getting great speed from the modem and had no issues with it at all. My ISP was able to set it up remotely in about 30 minutes. All the "experts" say it is best to have your own equipment, rather than rent from an ISP. I like that idea, but the only problem is that if equipment fails, you are responsible for it, whereas if you rent from the ISP, they replace any defective equipment at no cost. Also if you need an equipment upgrade, the ISP covers that too. I don't expect to need an upgrade as this will handle the fastest speeds being offered now by my ISP (1 Gbps), although not yet in my area. Right now I have 300 Mbps and the modem handles it nicely without any problem. This modem does NOT use the Puma chipset, which was causing some issues. This is a great
piece of equipment and suitable for home or business. Just has 4 lights (power on, upload, download and connected to internet). I thought I had seen comments about the lights being dim, but they are nice and bright; maybe bright enough to almost be distracting at times. Am very happy so far with the modem and would buy one again if it lasts well over time. There are a couple other modems by other quality manufacturers that are somewhat comparable to this one, but in side by side comparisons this seems to rate a little better. The Arris brand was recommended to me and it is the brand used by my ISP.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White

text_fidelity_a:
CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White) I purchased these for the RM650x in my new build. to clean up the appearance of my case, as the default Corsair cables are serviceable but neither flexible nor visually appealing. Do I have a fancy case? It's a Fractal Define Mini C, so, sorta. Do I have a side window? No. Will anyone ever see the interior of this case aside from me and randos and I'm flexing on? Certainly not.

Why get cables like these? Call it an eccentricity. I don't like chaos hiding right out of sight. Sure, the Mini C would have the outward appearance of a stocky monolith of unalloyed order, but inside there would be a twisting madness of PVC and copper, heaving silently against the surface. There would be no evidence of it, sure, but I would know.

I would know.

So anyway, I purchased these to extend the relentless teleology of the IC into the broader world, and to this end I was successful. The cables are much more flexible than the default ones and the paracord is an interesting contrast against the typical circuit boards and enameled aluminum panels. They are a bit pricey for what you get, that's definitely the case - you might be better served by getting a different brand or shorter extensions rather than the full PSU set. I just happened to have the money for the CableMods.

Caveats: if you are using velcro ties inside the case, then you have to be careful with the ModFlex, as the hook-side can pull threads from it. I presume ModMesh, being nylon, would not have that issue. to get around it, I used rubber/silicon bands, since unlike zipties they can be removed and adjusted relatively easily.

Would I recommend them? If you have a side-window or transparent case, they are a definitely aesthetically on point. ModFlex or ModMesh, either should be suitable. If not, unless you too are eccentric, it probably isn't worth it. The improvement in airflow and the reduction in strain on the components are minimal so long as you are implementing reasonable cable management techniques. I'm still happy I purchased them though, since I'm pretty sure I'll be able to use them in the next two-three builds and they did make it a bit easier to get everything where I wanted it.
text_fidelity_b: CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White)

They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am.

Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded.

Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed.

if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY

But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it.

I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos.

Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive.

Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle.

Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb It is harder and harder to find any radio that has an AM radio band on it, let alone a really good one. It is also rather difficult to find a decent radio that is not digitally tuned and controlled. This radio is a good solid radio with both of the above features on it.

WHAT IS THIS RADIO LIKE?
This radio is a good solid radio. It has a slide switch under the tuning bar which has three settings - OFF, AM, and FM. On the right side are two dials. There is one with volume that goes from Minimum to Maximum. The other dial is the tuning dial. That makes the tuning bar slide up and down for both AM and FM. There is a handle on top that flips up or goes down. There is a pull out telescopic antenna on the top for better reception. There is a place in the left side where you plug in the electric cord, but you can remove it if you prefer to operate solely by batteries. The cord is a little over 5 feet long. The plug is a two pronged plug and is polarized. There is a door on the back which slides off and allows you to put in 3 AA batteries. The door has attached hinges so you don't have to worry about losing the battery door off of the unit unless it breaks.

HOW DOES THIS RADIO PERFORM?
For AM I would say that it has okay reception It is not WOW but it is not terrible either. Since AM is not really dominating the airwaves anymore, I imagine that some people would not find this to be a problem. If you want really strong AM reception, this is okay, but you might be able to find better.

For FM reception, the radio is great. It pulls in quite a few stations and also plays them very clearly. The speaker is best showcased by FM. It is a full sound and impressive considering the size of the speaker and the basic nature of the radio. I found that it is a nice sound and enjoyable.

HANDLE
The handle has a bit of a recoil to help it snap back into place, but it does seem just a little bit flimsy to me. I wish it was just a bit sturdier. It is not enough to take off a star.

WHAT WOULD THIS RADIO COME IN HANDY FOR?
For those of you who are from the era where radios of this nature were commonplace, I am not writing this comment section for you. You already know what this would be good for. For those of you who think that In Tune, or other internet radio stations would suffice for any AM or FM radio stations, I would like to mention that during weather crises, that AM/FM and shortwave radio tend to be the only reception you can get if any. That includes disasters. At that point, internet is not an option, so it is important to have a back up communication capability to keep up on what is going on and any emergency information that might come up, or even information about upcoming help.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This radio is handy. It is a decent size, sturdy, and a solid basic radio. It gets decent reception and has a nice speaker which is especially nice for FM. During emergencies and times of crises, this is a good backup to have should internet not be an option. Running on both electricity and AA batteries, this would be a great addition to your basic emergency kit.

MY RATING
Despite the handle being a bit flimsier than I would like, it is still decent and a solid radio. I do not think that it is worth taking off a star.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

SAMSUNG T7 Portable SSD 500GB - Up to 1050MB/s - USB 3.2 External Solid State Drive, Blue (MU-PC500H/AM) I'm currently using this with my NextcloudPi setup to store my own data over the network. The Raspberry Pi4 supports USB 3.0, which this SSD also does. That's one of the main things I look for when hounding an SSD: fast transfer rates, as well as large capacity.
I know Samsung has a good reputation for SSD storage; I was very excited when this came in the mail. After re-installing NextcloudPi, I let the setup wizard reformat the Samsung T7 into Btrfs. The T7 formated flawlessly, and the storage shows up completely on both my web panel and my web settings.

I had to restart my Pi4 a few times, and each time I shot some items to my SSD for testing. I noticed it was pretty slow on boot, but after a few hours it seemed to read and write almost as fast as my previous SSD. I supposed, over time, it will adjust to the Pi4. My previous drive was a Verbatim USB SSD, also 3.0. That thing got HOT. It was also made of aluminum on the outside, and I was afraid this T7 would be the same. So far so good; it remains much cooler than the Verbatim.

text_fidelity_a:
ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.

text_fidelity_a:
HAYLOU True Wireless Earbuds, GT1 Bluetooth 5.0 Sports HD Stereo Touch Control Ear Buds with IPX5 Waterproof/Fast Connection/Mini Case(Only 30g)/Total 12H Playtime (Dark Grey) I’ve tested a few similar sets of ear buds with mixed results but I was really impressed with this set.

I read the instruction manual - removed the tiny stickers on each ear bud and plugged in the case. It achieved a full charge in just over an hour.

I removed the ear buds from the case, the right one first and then the left and they paired with each other immediately. I went to my Bluetooth settings in my iPhone and found Haylou-GT1_R and my phone paired with the set with no issue.

I was surprised at the sound quality these tiny ear buds deliver. They can definitely be turned up as loud as you’d want to listen. The bass, midtones and treble is on par for ear buds - even those that are much larger.

I did figure out that the initial way I had them in my ears was upside down when I went to test the calling features. The microphone needs to be pointed towards your mouth for best audio reception and sound quality improves a bit in this position.

Call quality was excellent for both hearing the other person and them hearing you.

In my testing the earbuds had no problem receiving within the 33’ stated range (actually making it to around 40’) and even received clearly through multiple walls - 2 rooms away with the doors closed and many obstacles in between.

The only issue I struggled with was tapping the ear bud to stop / start the music and answer / end calls / activate voice assistant and skip tracks. There is no button, you just tap an area of the exterior of the ear bud but you have to tap a very exact area which isn’t necessary easy to locate as it is not differentiated from the rest. It would have been helpful if the manufacturer put a different texture in that area so you could feel it with your finger to locate it.

While the manufacturers claims these last for 12 hours I found it was closer to 8 under normal use - still excellent. And the case will charge them without it having to be plugged back in which is always a nice feature.

These earbuds excelled in all of my tests showing that they are a high quality, dependable product.

This is a set I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend.

⭐️As with all Drew’s Reviews, if I discover something new about this product - good or bad - I will UPDATE my review. I believe in creating detailed, complete reviews because, like you, I depend on them when I am shopping. If you found my review HELPFUL - please click ⬇️ below!⭐️
text_fidelity_b: HAYLOU True Wireless Earbuds, GT1 Bluetooth 5.0 Sports HD Stereo Touch Control Ear Buds with IPX5 Waterproof/Fast Connection/Mini Case(Only 30g)/Total 12H Playtime (Dark Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black Bose is primarily known for their active noise canceling (ANC) phones though they have for years offered non-ANC phones. This is my first pair of Bose phones that are not in the ANC class of headphones and my impression of them is mostly positive. I do see some room for improvement, though.

First off, these are without question the lightest headphones (aside from ear buds) that I have ever worn. I am a bit odd in that I actually prefer heavier headphones but this is strictly a preference, not a criticism. In spite of the weight, the phones fit very nicely and do not feel like they're about to slip off if you lean down. This is not to say they're tight, but they are tight enough to hold well. They're easy to adjust too, so getting them to fit just right is simple enough. If exceptionally lightweight headphones are your thing, this is what you want.

The cord is a little different than other phones I have used in that the jacks on either end are of different sizes. This is good and bad. It's good in that there's no question of how to attach the cord because it only fits one way. But, it also means that a normal cord that comes with practically any other headphone will not work.

The sound quality is definitely better than average but not perfect (certainly not audiophile-level). The sound spectrum seems to be fairly well balanced. The highs are good and the "edges" are crisp and clean for most tracks. The midrange is ok but slightly hollow. The bass is very good without being overdriven. One of the problems with a lot of headphones is that they tend to overdrive the bass which is fine if you really like your bass, but too much can overpower the rest of the spectrum and give some of us headaches. That these phones do not over-amplify the bass is a pleasant surprise.

Having a pair of Bose QC-15 ANC phones, I can compare the two models' sound profiles and there are some slight differences. Where the QC-15s are great at the highs and overdrive the bass, the midrange is sorely lacking. The SoundTrue get the bass right and have good highs but fall slightly short on the midrange (though still better than the QC-15s). Comparing just the sound profiles and ignoring the ANC function, I prefer the SoundTrue over the QC-15s.

The carrying case is nice and should provide some protection when packed for travel. I would have preferred a slightly harder and more crush-resistant case but that's me being picky. There's not a lot of extra room in the case so storage is not really an option with the case.

The price is a little high ($180 as I write this) and that might be a little steep for some. It comes down to whether a less expensive set of phones delivers the same (or better) sound profile.

My overall impression of the Bose SoundTrue headphones is positive. These are very comfortable and exceptionally lightweight and the sound quality is good though not perfect. These phones are above average and are worth consideration if you want non-ANC headphones or if you're looking for very lightweight headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black
