text_fidelity_a:
ZUMIMALL Security Cameras Wireless Outdoor-2K Home Security Camera Battery Powered, Outdoor Security Cameras with 3MP Color Night Vision/Spotlight/IP66 Waterproof/PIR Detection/2-Way Talk/Cloud/SD I have been testing and reviewing WiFi cameras for the last five years. Over that time the industry has seen major advances which has led to incredible availability of high quality cameras at very reasonable costs. I have tested nearly 100 cameras and it takes a bit to impress me but I must say this set did just that.

I had no problem setting this camera up on my network. I set it both up after fully charging them in about a half hour with no issues.

Due to security precautions I never use cloud based storage in relation to WiFi cameras because that amount of constant data transfer opens your network to unnecessary hacking. The only cameras that I employ in my home allow for local storage - whether to a dedicated hard drive or individual micro SD held within each camera. This camera can hold up to a 128GB micro SD card. The card will over write the oldest data first - how much footage the card holds is dictated by the settings you select. Due to the fact these cameras only record when motion is detected a 128GB card will hold quite a lot and should suffice for 99% of people.

It’s important to know that by default the camera is set to record and save to the cloud. That can easily be reset in preference settings. In addition if you don’t install a micro SD card your camera will only capture still images when viewing - if you don’t have two extra micro SD cards order two when purchasing this set.

The camera provides a crystal clear 1080p footage and I found the motion activation very responsive. With my mesh WiFi network I encountered no lag in viewing - typically camera lag has to do with individual network properties rather than the camera itself.

The batteries in these cameras are phenomenal and actually last as long as is claimed in the listing. The battery’s life will be dictated by how often the camera is activated by motion but I have had both cameras installed and running now for over 2 months without having to recharge yet.

In my tests I found this to be an excellent budget friendly WiFi camera set that as long as you utilize the micro SD card feature is quite secure. Not having to run power cables is a major advantage and will allow these to be placed in far more places. The internal batteries are excellent and are sure to impress. The app is well designed, intuitive and easy to use even for beginners.

This is an all around excellent set of wireless WiFi cameras that I have recommended and do to you as well.

Thanks for reading my review. I enjoy writing them as I value reading other’s reviews when I’m making a buying decision. I regularly update my reviews to reflect any changes I may discover and to include helpful tips you may need if you purchase the product. I will always make every effort to answer any questions I can as it is my pleasure to help.
text_fidelity_b: ZUMIMALL Security Cameras Wireless Outdoor-2K Home Security Camera Battery Powered, Outdoor Security Cameras with 3MP Color Night Vision/Spotlight/IP66 Waterproof/PIR Detection/2-Way Talk/Cloud/SD

bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100) I got this for my teenaged son to use on his gaming PC. He had actually broken his previous gaming headphones and this seemed like a no-frills decent replacement for him to try.
The sound quality is actually quite good. Both the ear pieces and the microphone are crisp and clear, so no complaints there. However my son found it a little uncomfortable to wear compared to his larger over-the-ear style headphones before. The actual ear parts on this are smaller, which means they don't fully envelop your ears the way other ones do. On the plus side, this means it doesn't block as much external noise, which I like for him in our household (no more calling his name when he can't us!), but others may want more noise isolation. Also, the smaller ear pieces aren't as comfortable when worn as the larger ones.
I also didn't like that it didn't come with an adapter to break out for mic and speakers like other headsets do. I thought it would come with that as an option, as I've never gotten a PC headset that didn't offer either a splitter or TRRS combo adapter so you can use it with both a laptop that has mic/headphone combos as well as separate mic and headphone jacks commonly found on a desktop.
Thankfully I had an extra one lying around for him to use, so that wasn't an issue. But something to take into consideration. Others, I've got to give it at least 4 stars for working well and doing what it should. But there might be other options for the price worth considering as well if you want larger earphones or a breakout cable included.
text_fidelity_b: bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100)

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9) Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back.

This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small.

There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.)

Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care.

The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before.

The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost.

Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal.

In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.)

It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there.

I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9)

Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop I know, you are probably thinking- what kind of idiot would try this on their LAP? I can not tell you who, but let's just say I am a witness.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This little stand folds perfectly flat. It comes in a drawstring bag which keeps it from attacking you. You see, this is VERY easy to pinch your fingers in. I have the bruises to prove it. However, once I figured it out, I was able to avoid it any more. Keeping this in the case is a GOOD thing.

HOW TO USE THIS
When I first got this, I was explaining to a certain someone that this was to keep the laptop cooler and hold it at a better angle. It was not until that certain someone was carrying on about what a stupid device it was that I realized that this someone was trying to use it on their lap. Don't do that. You won't like it.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
There are silicone pads and 3 settings for this stand. The pads hold the laptop in place and the stand in each setting. It holds a lightweight laptop well and the angles are good. I found using it on the right table top helps. It seems to stay put well, but if you have a really slick top, you can always put a non-skid pad under the whole thing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you are careful and only use this on the table top and are careful about not pinching your fingers, this is a nice little stand. It holds pretty well and is at a decent angle so far for our lightweight laptop.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. It is hard to use unless you really pay attention because it can suddenly fold down pinching the fingers, so I took a star off for that. It is a nice stand so far, but I will update as we try other laptops on it over time if necessary to let you know if something changes.
text_fidelity_b: Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player The Roku Premiere player is easy to set up and has a well-designed user interface that requires no reference to a user manual. I connected it to the tv (using an HDMI cable), plugged it in, turned on the tv and selected the appropriate source. I was disappointed that there was no option to plug in a network cable for a wired connection (like there is for the Fire TV box; you have to go up to the Premiere+ to get that port). This might be a concern for anyone with a weak or problematic wifi signal.

The initialization was fairly simple: language selection, wifi connection (it supports AC as well as N), automatic detection of the tv display type, automatic software update, then a separate session on the computer to register the device and create a Roku account. I had another disappointment here: the account creation requires the entry of payment info, either credit card or Paypal. If I want to use the box just to watch my subscribed services, such as Netflix and Amazon, there's no reason for me to give Roku any payment information at all, it just increases the risk of malicious use. (If you really don't like this, you can sign up using a Paypal account, then go back into your Paypal account and rescind the Roku permissions.)

After that it was all plain sailing, and I had no complaints: streaming video was clear and glitch-free, the sound was good. All in all, a very nice streaming box for a reasonable price. For my money, however, I would consider upgrading to the Premiere+. Or, the Fire TV box, which is what I normally use at home.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player

I subsequently purchased a Nikon D70s camera (1,000,000 times better camera) and this flash is great for extremely dark shots on that camera (though the built-in flash is perfect for fill so this is really only for night shots and shots in darkness where I want to get something far away).  If you own a CoolPix camera, consider buying a used flash that isn't as powerfull. text_fidelity_a:
Belkin PowerHouse Dual Lightning Charging Dock for iPad Air, iPad Air 2, iPad 4th Gen, iPad mini 4, iPad mini 3, iPad mini 2, iPad mini, iPhone 6S / 6S Plus, iPhone 6 / 6 Plus, iPhone 5 / 5S / 5c, and iPod touch 7th Gen When I was reading about this product, I was intrigued. The Belkin charging dock duo can charge two devices: an IPAD (4th generation), IPAD Mini/AIR, Nano (7th generation), IPOD Touch (5th generation) or an Iphone (5 or up), at the same time. Surely this is a useful item to own. Well, I was mistaken.

Usefulness: While you would think that this product is useful....because it can charge multiple devices at once... it is also a little burdensome. It's bulky, so I would not recommend this product while traveling. On the other hand, if you use the charging cables/cords that come with the devices, you can wrap them up and store them in a small compartment in your bag. This docking station would take up space in a travel bag, briefcase or suitcase. However, I would recommend this product for those who want to charge multiple "I" devices on their nightstand or dressers. I do like that they can be charged standing up, which makes them neater and more orderly. On a positive note, you can use your device while it is charging. Why you would want to I don't know, but it is an option.

Functionality: There is a handy, dandy ball that you can roll with your finger that allows you to raise and lower the adapter (front compartment and back), in order to accommodate a phone with a cover. The instructions suggest that you remove the cover to charge, but for the average consumer that would be inconvenient to remove the cover every time you want to dock it. Regardless, if you have a thick cover (i.e., Otterbox or Reiko) it will not fit on the docking station no matter how much you adjust it. So you must remove the thicker covers (like Otterbox) before you can dock it. My son complained that this was a hassle/extremely inconvenient, especially when he can leave his cover on and simply plug it into the wall. He didn't think that removing the cover to charge outweighed the inconvenience of removing it. However, a slimmer case (less protective ones), like those decorative/fashion ones (i.e., Kate Spade, etc) will fit on the Belkin.

Cost: $82 is very expensive for a product that isn't a must have or at least one that is useful. I am not sure that this product would be a good investment.

Overall, I give the Belkin Power House Dual Charge and Sync Docking station 2.5 out of 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin PowerHouse Dual Lightning Charging Dock for iPad Air, iPad Air 2, iPad 4th Gen, iPad mini 4, iPad mini 3, iPad mini 2, iPad mini, iPhone 6S / 6S Plus, iPhone 6 / 6 Plus, iPhone 5 / 5S / 5c, and iPod touch 7th Gen

Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US) The Targus VuScape Protective cover and stand is a pretty good, helpful aid for those who own an Apple Ipad2. It features a thin, lightweight design that is meant to hold the iPad2 snugly in place while you work.

Having a stand for your iPad is certainly a good idea and I like that this stand can be used to position your iPad in different ways. There are multiple grooves so that you can display your iPad at different angles. The cover can also be folded back completely, allowing the consumer to hold the iPad in the hands without the stand.

This protective cover/stand does have some nice features to offer, but after using it for a while, it is more than apparent that the stand is not perfect. Probably the greatest issue is that the stand isn't as sturdy as I would prefer. If you use the stand on a solid, flat surface, you shouldn't have too many problems, but place it on other surfaces and it tends to bend just a little bit. The slightest bend will cause the grooves to give way just a little, and the iPad will no longer be securely held in place.

I generally like the thin, lightweight design of this stand, but the thinness possibly goes a tad far. If the manufacturer had made this stand just a little bit thicker, it would be stronger and more likely to hold the iPad in place without any problems. I suppose this is the trade- off one must make when selecting a stand such as this. Lightweight is nice, especially for something like an iPad, but lightweight means the stand is lacking in strength.

All in all, this is a good stand and certainly worth considering, but not a deluxe stand like I expected. Again, as long as you are willing to sacrifice sturdiness for lightweight design, you should be fine. And try to use only on the flattest surfaces for the best results. Follow these guidelines and you should find yourself reasonably happy with this protective cover and stand from Targus.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US)

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black) The wide angle lens is wonderful. The field of view and the speed (light gathering ability) of the lens can only be rivaled by high end camera and lens combinations costing six to ten times as much (admittedly those are superior in many other ways as well). Still, the point is that no other compact point and shoot camera can rival the field of view and speed of this one. Nevertheless, some things come up short of fair on the LX3.

The shutter lag is terrible. I am a very instinctive shooter that is quite capable in photojournalist style candids but I am almost always defeated by this camera.

I am not a photophile or electronic gadget spec sheet bench racer. I've done wonderful 8x10 prints with a 6MP camera and 10MP is enough to get prints after substantial cropping. I have huge film scans when I need them but I cannot realistically show dozens of megapixels on screen or in print for more than a handful of images. I also shoot in .jpg and it's great. I can't imagine the agony of terabytes of raw data jamming my PC.

I love the LX3 video quality for movies. It's ideal for Youtube and even Youtube HD. I do not like the Quicktime .MOV format or the weak compression algorithm. I wish it had H.264 and wrote an .MPG type format. It still beats the data format from a DVD camcorder though.

The audio quality for movies is terrible. Again, I'm not talking audiophile critique here. For comparison, my Sony DSC T9 (ultra compact point and shoot) has far better sound.

I hate the manual aspect ratio slider. If I shoot movies I want 16:9 but for stills I want 3:2 (of course). The LX3 requires that I remember to both turn the dial and slide the switch or I will end up shooting 16:9 stills.

Overall, it's a great camera. I hope they get the rest sorted out by the time I expect to buy another one in about 3 or 4 years.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black)

text_fidelity_a: OURLINK 600Mbps Mini 802.11ac Dual Band 2.4G/5G Wireless Network Adapter USB Wi-Fi Dongle Adapter with 5dBi Antenna Support Win Vista,Win 7,Win 8.1, Win 10,Mac OS X 10.9-10.15 The adapter installed without a problem in one of my Win10 machines and the utility software is versatile.  I’ve found the range and stability to be excellent and have a strong signal through two walls and one floor at the opposite end of the house.  I get nearly every bit of the 250 Mbps coming to my house from my ISP. The adapter’s high gain antenna -- which, at 15 cm, is longer than the picture in the product description at the time of my purchase -- is likely responsible for much of the observed performance.
